sentences.text: Rati Ram vs State Of Haryana on 9 April, 2025

Author: Sanjay Kumar
Bench: Sanjay Kumar

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal No. Of 2025
 (@ Slp(C) No. 5123/2023)
 Rati Ram & Ors. Appe
 Versus
 State Of Haryana & Ors. Resp
 O R D E R
1. Leave granted.

2. By the impugned judgment dated 02.08.2022, the Punjab and Haryana High Court affirmed the rejection of the claim of the appellants for enhanced compensation, on the ground that the application filed by them under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, the Act of 1894) was beyond the prescribed period of six months.

3. It is, however, an admitted fact that in relation to lands in a neighboring village covered by the very same notification issued under Section 4(1) of the Act of 1894, the land owners were awarded much higher compensation on the basis of the valuation per acre being put at 3,43,25,310/- per acre and after deducting development charges, quantified at 15 percent, the land value was determined as 2,91,76,530/-.
4.
In the light of this development and as the appellants would SWETA BALODI Date: 2025.04.17 16:00:59 IST Reason:

have been at liberty to avail the benefit of Section 28A of the Act of 1894, had they not filed the belated application under Section 18 of the Act of 1894, we are inclined to accept the claim of the appellants.

The appeal is accordingly allowed, directing the respondents to pay compensation to the appellants also at the same rate as was extended to the landowners of the neighboring village, i.e.,
2,91,76,530/- per acre, along with all consequential statutory benefits.
Interest would be payable to the appellants on the enhanced amount only from the date of such enhancement in relation to the lands in the neighbouring village.
The balance compensation due and payable in terms of this order shall be disbursed to the appellants within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
